This work suits people who are meticulous, patient, and enjoy interacting with others. If you can tell whether a patient's statement that they cannot see clearly reflects a prescription problem or an eye disease and can crouch down to examine a child, this field suits you.

Optometrists are eye-care professionals with systematic training in optometry. They perform vision examinations and clinical refraction, prescribe glasses and contact lenses, assess visual function, screen for common eye diseases, and provide guidance on myopia prevention and eye-health management.

paragraphs: The day begins with the first patient: measuring visual acuity, performing refraction, asking about symptoms, and examining the fundus. One complete workflow for one patient takes about twenty minutes. During peak seasons, such as the start of school and winter or summer breaks, there is barely time to drink water. During slower periods, optometrists calibrate equipment and count inventory. Cases involving presbyopia, strabismus, or adolescent myopia require more time for planning and communication.
